title: Allow to change a Dashboards Layout Mode in hindsight
summary: Dashboard Layout Mode should be able to be changeable in hindsight. There are edge cases that need a logic for transferring the dashlets, though. See #15 As a workaround, users could the move Dashlets one by one to another dashlet. But this would be very tedious especially with many DAshlets to transfer.

title: Ghost presses & workarounds
summary: The touch panel sometimes reports presses nobody made. There is no fix yet; this issue collects what is known and what helps. So far I am the only user affected, on one board. ## What happens - Presses appear with nothing touching the screen, mostly in a band down the middle of it. - They come singly or in bursts. In a burst the device is basically unusable. - A ghost press lasts about as long as a real tap (100–160 ms measured, against 60–100 ms for real taps), so it can't be filtered out by duration. - Holding the bare board by its edges triggers them. In the printed case on a power bank they are fewer, but still occur. - They got worse during a longer session, with some moisture on the device. Wiping the screen did not obviously help then. ## What helps most **Plug in the USB cable with no fingers anywhere near the touchscreen.** Hold only the very bottom of the printed case and touch nothing else. This is by far the biggest improvement. Plugging in with a finger on the touchscreen immediately gives ghost presses, right from startup. Theory: the touch controller takes its "no finger" baseline at power-up, so a finger on or near the display at that moment gives it a bad baseline. ## Other workarounds (none confirmed to fix it) - **If a burst starts:** unplug, wait a few seconds, and plug in again as above. - **Try a different USB cable.** - **Use a power bank** instead of a computer or hub (to be confirmed: one run had no ghosts on a power bank, a later one had two). - **Wipe the screen clean** if it gets worse during use. ## Tried, no noticeable improvement - A silica gel sachet inside the case. - Reading the panel on its interrupt pin instead of polling. ## What we know about the cause - The controller is a CST816D. Its documentation lists no setting for touch sensitivity or noise filtering in normal scanning; that tuning appears to be fixed in the chip's firmware by the module maker. - The chip's datasheet says the sensing is sensitive to grounding
